Reads rfc8878.txt several times upfront and creates a dedicated task to 'understand the zstd format completely'; three consecutive section reads precede the main Write — deliberate, front-loaded spec study rather than reactive skimming.
After the initial Write, ~50 Edit/Bash/Read debugging cycles with NO further RFC reads — spec understanding was never deepened or re-checked per subsystem during implementation of the hard areas.
Explores test files/sizes and output diffs but shows no hexdump of an actual .zst frame to cross-check byte layout/bit-ordering against the spec — no observed byte-level grounding.

reasoning: The agent did meaningful upfront orientation — reading the scaffold and reading RFC 8878 several times with an explicit comprehension task — which clears the level-3 'reactive skim' anchor. But the reading was entirely front-loaded: no RFC re-consultation occurs across the long debugging arc, and there is no visible byte-layout/hex-dump inspection of real frames to confirm tricky rules, which the level-5 anchor expects. That places observed behavior between 3 and 5, closer to 4. Confidence is low because the trajectory file contains only tool-call headers, so comprehension quality cannot be directly verified.
